result.title: SPARE: Sparsity Allocation via Routing Entropy for Efficient MoEs
result.summary: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architectures scale model capacity efficiently, yet their substantial memory footprint poses a major barrier to deployment. Expert pruning reduces this footprint, but most methods focus on which experts to remove and prune every layer equally. We propose SPARE (Sparsity Allocation via Routing Entropy), a training-free, selector-agnostic method that decides how many experts to remove from each layer using routing entropy, the entropy of tokens' normalized Top-K gate weights on calibration data. When a token's gate weight is spread evenly, removing one active expert discards little of it, so SPARE prunes layers with more diffuse routing more aggressively. A perturbation bound under random pruning formalizes this intuition, and controlled interventions with a fixed selector link concentrated routing to larger output changes. With the same selector and budget, SPARE improves average accuracy over uniform allocation on Mixtral, Qwen3, and DeepSeek models, especially at high pruning ratios. At 50% expert pruning, it raises the eight-task average of Qwen3-30B-A3B from 57.2% to 63.8%, and the math, code, and science average of DeepSeek-R1 from 80.1 to 82.8.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 SPARE：一种免训练、与选择器无关的 MoE 专家剪枝方法，用校准数据上 token 归一化 Top-K 门控权重的路由熵衡量各层路由的弥散程度，对路由更均匀（冗余更高）的层剪得更激进，并给出随机剪枝下的扰动界与干预实验支持。
AI.relevance_reason: 「按信息弥散度决定各层容量/计算削减量」可作为一种分配信号的线索，供核查能否用于 LVR 中逐层 latent 更新或动态计算预算的取舍；但原文不涉及多模态推理状态、证据筛选或停止决策，迁移仅为推测。
